title: Fewest Wildcards in a Common Pattern
body:
A pattern is a string of lowercase letters and ? wildcards (each ? matches any one letter). Two patterns intersect if the wildcards can be filled so both produce the same string. Given n patterns of equal length, find the minimum number of ? a pattern can contain while still intersecting all of them.

Function to complete

Complete minQuestionMarks(patterns). It returns the fewest '?' in a pattern that intersects all of them.

  • patterns: the patterns, all of the same length

Input reading and printing are handled for you, like on LeetCode. The input format below is what the tests and Custom input use.
inp: The first line is n. Each of the next n lines is one pattern.
out: The value your function returns (the driver prints it): the fewest ? characters a pattern intersecting all of them can have.
cons: All patterns have the same length m, 1 ≤ m ≤ 10<sup>3</sup>

samples.ex: Only the position holding r vs b differs between the two patterns, so one '?' there (for example hacker?ank) intersects both. Every other position has a single forced letter. The answer is 1.
The first column holds three different letters (a, b, c), so it needs a '?'. The second column is x everywhere. One '?' is enough.
